title: Thrice-Greatest Hermes, Vol. 1
author: G. R. S. Mead
description: Thrice-Greatest Hermes: Studies in Hellenistic Theosophy and Gnosis, Volume I: Prolegomena, by G. R. S. Mead (London and Benares: Theosophical Publishing Society, 1906). Mead's three-volume work was the first comprehensive English translation of the extant sermons and fragments of the Trismegistic literature, with commentaries and notes. This first volume is the prolegomena: a survey of the history and sources of the Hermetic tradition, the figure of Hermes-Thoth in Egyptian religion, Plutarch on Isis and Osiris, the Naassene document and its Hermetic hymns, the Poimandres tradition, the relationship of the Hermetica to Philo, Gnosticism and Neoplatonism, and testimony from Church Fathers and Arabic writers. Combining Theosophical sympathy with serious scholarship, it profoundly influenced twentieth-century Western esotericism, Jung and literary modernism, and frames the library's Hermetic texts.
